<<NOTES ON WHITEWASHING A CELLAR WALL>>

WHITEWASHING A CELLAR WALL IS A COMMON PRACTICE TO PREVENT MOLD AND DUST FROM BUILDUP. IT IS DONE BY APPLYING A THIN LAYER OF WHITEWASH OVER THE WALL SURFACE. THIS PROCESS HELPED TO MAKE THE WALLS LOOK CLEANER AND MORE PRECIOUS. THE WHITEWASH IS MADE FROM A MIXTURE OF LIME AND WATER, WHICH IS THEN APPLYING TO THE WALL. THIS PROCESS IS IMPORTANT FOR THE LONG-TERM HEALTH OF THE BUILDING. THE WHITEWASH CAN BE APPLIED IN THE AFTERNOON TO PREVENT THE SUN FROM DRYING IT OUT. IT IS ALSO A WAY TO PRESERVE THE STRUCTURE OF THE WALL. THE WHITEWASH CAN BE APPLIED IN SECTIONS TO MAKE IT EASIER TO CLEAN. IT IS IMPORTANT TO MAKE SURE THE WHITEWASH IS DRY BEFORE USING IT FOR OTHER PURPOSES. THE WHITEWASH CAN BE APPLIED WITH A WET SPANISH OR A WET SPANISH TROWEL. IT IS A SIMPLE AND ECONOMICAL WAY TO KEEP THE CELLAR CLEAN AND SAFE.
